movable_0._comment_timing: One integration step per control tick, across ticks, in per-second units (with n_sub sub-steps). BY DESIGN — see EMBODIED_DDM_PLAN.md Section 0.3. Do not add internal relaxation steps.

embodied_pure_ddm._comment_structure: --- structure. K == 2 ONLY: the pure DDM is the SPRT for a binary hypothesis test, and there is no scalar log-likelihood ratio for K > 2. For K > 2 use moving_behavior 'embodied_ddm' with accumulator_mode 'race' (the MSPRT). Exactly 2 target_ids are required; their order fixes the sign of x (+z favours the first). ---
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_num_neurons: Only sizes the SHARED detection ring so perception is bit-identical to the ring attractor. The DDM never reads it to decide.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_evidence: --- evidence. eta_rate is a noise RATE: eta_i = eta_rate_i/sqrt(dt), so c^2 = sum of squares and results are tick-rate independent (Section 1.3). ---
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_evidence_mode: difference (default; the SPRT when eta_rate entries are equal) | llr (precision-weighted; needs the deferred per-target uncertainty field and currently raises).
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_dist_mode: Shared with embodied_ddm and applied to q BEFORE sampling. none (default, matches the ring attractor) | exp | subtense | loom. Any non-none setting makes A time-varying and invalidates the closed-form ER/DT of Section 3.1.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_attention_mode: none (default) | vonmises | saccade. Shared with embodied_ddm.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_extended: Across-trial variability ([B06] Section 3): s_A > 0 gives slow errors, s_x > 0 gives fast errors. NOTE s_A > 0 is one of the assumptions whose violation JUSTIFIES collapsing bounds (Section 4.2), so it is theoretically linked to boundary_mode, not independent of it.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_boundary: --- boundary. WARNING: threshold_policy bayes_risk / reward_rate give the optimal CONSTANT boundary. They do NOT justify a collapsing boundary — under their own assumptions the constant boundary is provably optimal (Section 4.1, Appendix C). Combining them with boundary_mode 'collapsing' logs a warning and stamps boundary_policy_incoherent into the record; never report that combination as optimal. ---
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_threshold_policy: manual | bayes_risk | reward_rate | geometric. Coherent with collapsing: manual (descriptive) and geometric (derived) only.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_cost_ratio: c_e/c_tau. ONE parameter: only the ratio affects argmin BR (Section 3.3). Ignored under the geometric policy, which derives both costs from geometry.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_T0: Non-decision time = MEASURED actuator lag, not a fitted nuisance parameter. The decision latches internally on crossing and reaches the motors T0 seconds later.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_threshold_update_ticks: 0 = compute z* once at evidence onset; >0 = recompute every N ticks. Under geometric, z* is state-dependent (d and Delta change as the agent moves) so >0 is the meaningful setting — but do not combine a recomputed z* with an explicit collapse_form without logging both.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_geometric_error_mode: terminal_graded (c_e = A/lambda_t; rho = (A/c)^2 * c_e / c_tau(Delta), so rho ~ A^3) | terminal_categorical (options differ in kind, 0-1 loss: c_e = cost_ratio, rho = (A/c)^2 * cost_ratio / c_tau(Delta) with c_tau = 2 sin^2(Delta/4)). The error mode sets c_e ONLY; c_tau is shared with the other modes and carries ALL the angular dependence, hence the entire collapse. | correctable (c_e = 2 d sin(Delta/2)/v; rho ~ A^2 and DOES produce an arrival deadline).
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_lambda_t: Opportunity cost of time in QUALITY UNITS PER SECOND (the currency of Charnov's marginal value theorem). Only read under terminal_graded. <float> = use directly; null = analytic default E[q]*v/E[d] resolved at evidence onset; "mvt" = the marginal-value fixed point, where iteration k reads lambda_t_measured fed back from run k-1 and iteration 0 falls back to the analytic default. rho ~ 1/lambda_t, so a RICHER environment gives a LOWER threshold and faster, sloppier decisions — the MVT prediction, and worth a sweep of its own. IGNORED under terminal_categorical (lambda_t enters rho only through c_e, and the categorical c_e is cost_ratio), so do not set it in that mode.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_delta_min: Clamp on the angular separation: sin^2(Delta/4) -> 0 sends rho -> inf (targets in the same direction means deliberation is free). Keeps sinh() from overflowing.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_A_source: Where the A entering rho AND z* comes from (it enters twice: rho ~ A^2*c_e/(c^2*c_tau) and z* = a*c^2/(2A)). Under the KNOWN-|A| model (TASK_A_KNOWN_DRIFT.md) only two options are coherent: 'ensemble' = A_expected, fixed for the whole block -- the agent knows the magnitude characteristic of its environment. A_expected is REQUIRED; there is no null -> running-mean fallback, which was undefined at evidence onset and made z* depend on trial history. 'oracle' = the true per-trial |q0-q1|; equivalent to ensemble in a fixed scenario and differing only if target qualities vary across trials, in which case it is an oracle assumption (calibration and V-tests only). 'online_evidence' (|x_t|/t) and 'online_lognormal' (|q0-q1|*exp(eps), eps ~ N(0,s^2), drawn once at onset) are ESTIMATION models: they infer |A| from the evidence and belong to TASK_B_UNKNOWN_DRIFT.md. They are REJECTED here unless drift_knowledge is set to 'estimated'. Under them `a` is no longer the log-odds at commitment and the collapse acquires a second source besides the geometry.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_evidence_target: quality (default) | net_value. Strictly, under an asymmetric layout the agent should accumulate net value q_i - lambda_t*d_i/v, since a nearer but slightly worse target can be the correct choice; net_value raises NotImplementedError for now and is irrelevant in the symmetric case.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_collapse_form: DERIVED: geometric (re-evaluates rho from the LIVE angular separation each tick — exact in both far and near field; under terminal_graded this gives a BOUNDED collapse toward z_floor_analytic, falling linearly in log-distance in the far field, and NOT a deadline) | deadline (numerical Frazier-Yu; under terminal_graded it is NO LONGER geometrically derivable and requires an explicit deadline_T). DESCRIPTIVE (fits to RT data, NO optimality argument): weibull | hyperbolic | exponential | linear. Keep the two categories separate in every claim.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_weibull_a_inf: 1.0 => no collapse, identical to boundary_mode static.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_deadline_T: null => derive from geometry (arrival time). The geometry supplies its own deadline, which is what makes the collapse derived rather than imposed.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_urgency_mode: off | boundary | gating. 'gating' low-pass filters the evidence and MULTIPLIES by urgency rather than integrating (Cisek et al.) — a genuinely different mechanism, NOT a reparameterisation of a collapsing bound.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_readout_mode: normalized (default; P1 = clip((1+x/z(t))/2,0,1), needs no drift estimate and sharpens automatically as a collapsing boundary closes) | posterior (P1 = sigmoid(2*A_hat*x/c^2); principled but presumes the agent knows the drift).
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_predecision_motion: average (default; belief-weighted heading — a gradual turn toward the leader as x accumulates; the setting comparable to the ring attractor's pre-bifurcation spatial averaging) | midpoint (FIXED angular bisector of the two BEARINGS while deliberating, independent of x, then a STEP to the chosen bearing on commitment; beliefs are still computed and logged, only the heading ignores them) | forward (belief-weighted heading, constant speed) | stationary (the NON-EMBODIED control: no translation and no rotation, so bearings never change and there is no feedback loop). NOTE: coupled to the geometric c_tau derivation — under stationary c_tau == 1 identically, and under midpoint c_tau = 1 - cos(Delta/2) is EXACT rather than a near-tie approximation.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_embodiment_arms: The embodiment loop has two arms: decision->motion (x influences the heading) and motion->threshold (pose changes Delta, which changes z* via rho(Delta)). stationary cuts both; midpoint cuts only the first; average keeps both. An effect present in average but not midpoint belongs to the first arm; one present in midpoint but not stationary belongs to the second.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_scaling_mode: concentration | constant | magnitude. Under midpoint, concentration == cos(Delta/2) and is PURELY GEOMETRIC: it carries no decision information and drives speed to zero as Delta -> pi, so the agent creeps to the midpoint and hovers until noise resolves the tie (the closest behavioural match to the ring attractor at a symmetric tie). Use constant to disable gating so midpoint does exactly one thing; use concentration deliberately if the hovering is the object of study.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_bisector_eps: Hold the previous heading when |sum of unit bearing vectors|/2 falls below this (Delta -> pi, where the vectors cancel and atan2(0,0) is undefined). A guard that fires repeatedly means the agent is parked between the targets — a result, not an error; it is logged per tick as bisector_guard_fired.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_c_expected: Noise-side counterpart of A_expected: the noise scale c the POLICY assumes, in evidence units (c^2 = sum of the per-target noise rates squared, so for two equal channels c = sqrt(2) * eta). null (default) = the true scale. A value != the true c is a deliberately MISSPECIFIED policy: the boundary, information rate and posterior are computed as if the sensor had that noise, while the evidence keeps its real noise (legacy eta_rate or the shared stream's white_rate). The paper's 'wrong noise model' sweep sets c_expected = f * c_true.

bifurcation._comment_mode: behavioral for ALL three models so switch counts and alignment events are measured by identical code.
